description: Retrieval over an entity graph and its community summaries, introduced by Microsoft Research, so both entity questions and whole-corpus questions can be answered.
A question about the whole corpus (themes, risks, trends). No single chunk holds the answer, so top-k retrieval fails.
A group of entities more densely connected to each other than to the rest of the graph.
Community detection where each node repeatedly adopts the label most common (or heaviest) among its neighbors until labels stop changing.
A modularity-optimizing community detection method that guarantees connected communities and builds a hierarchy. GraphRAG uses its hierarchical form.
A model-written title and summary of one community, generated from its own entities and relations at indexing time.
Answers questions about specific entities by fanning out to their neighborhood, related chunks and reports within a context budget.
Map batches of community reports to points rated 0-100, keep the best, and reduce them into one answer.
A GraphRAG mode that starts from community-level context and drills down into local search with follow-up questions.
